Visual reference and usage guide for every component and style used across this wiki.

The ## above is what every ## heading looks like automatically — no import needed. The XenoMarkers components give explicit control over the same shapes. SectionTab SectionBanner SubSectionBanner ### Subsection Name <SubSectionBanner /> GaugeHeaderright value

Most of the time ## headings are all you need. Use the explicit components when you need a tab label above a banner, a named sub-section break, or a gauge bar with a right-side value: import { SectionTab, SectionBanner, SubSectionBanner, GaugeHeader } from '@site/src/components/XenoMarkers'; <SectionTab>Optional</SectionTab> <SectionBanner>My Section</SectionBanner> ### Named Break <SubSectionBanner /> <GaugeHeader value="3/3">Progress Header</GaugeHeader>

Every component accepts a size prop that sets its font-size. All internal dimensions use em units so everything scales proportionally: <SectionBanner size="0.8rem">Smaller than default</SectionBanner> <SectionBanner size="1.5rem">Bigger than default</SectionBanner> <GaugeHeader size="1rem" value="done">Larger gauge</GaugeHeader> Default sizes: SectionTab → 0.72rem, SectionBanner → 1rem, SubSectionBanner → 1.25rem, GaugeHeader → 0.78rem.

The table of contents only picks up markdown ## headings — JSX components are invisible to it. If a section using an explicit component also needs a ToC entry, place a ## heading immediately before it: ## My Section <SectionBanner>My Section</SectionBanner> The CSS collapses the ## heading visually (the component shows instead) while keeping the anchor alive for the ToC link.
All card components share a dark frame with metallic-yellow rivets at each corner.

Settings Shows a screenshot inside the card frame with an optional floating pill label above it. src is passed through useBaseUrl automatically — use the /img/ path as-is. import { LocationCard } from '@site/src/components/LocationCard'; <LocationCard src="/img/settings-panel.png" title="Settings" /> <LocationCard src="/img/something.png" /> {/* no label */} The highlight prop annotates regions of the screenshot. Coordinates are fractions of the image (0–1). Highlighted regions pulse with a gold border; hovering fades them so the full image is visible. grow expands a region outward by that many pixels on every side: <LocationCard src="/img/panel.png" title="Panel" highlight={[ { l: 0.05, t: 0.1, w: 0.4, h: 0.15, text: "Name field" }, { l: 0.6, t: 0.7, w: 0.3, h: 0.2, text: "Save button", grow: 4 }, ]} />

⚠️Put a screenshot of the right-click menu here Right-click Menu Same frame and rivets as LocationCard, but shows a caution area instead of an image. Use it anywhere a screenshot is still needed and replace the whole tag with a <LocationCard> once the real image is ready. import { PlaceholderCard } from '@site/src/components/PlaceholderCard'; <PlaceholderCard title="Settings Panel" text="Put a screenshot of the Settings panel here" />

Anything here gets the riveted frame. Custom Content The raw frame primitive used by LocationCard and PlaceholderCard. Use it directly when you need the riveted frame around non-image content. Accepts title, style, className, frameClassName, labelClassName, frameStyle, labelStyle, and topSpacing="none" to suppress the margin reserved for the floating label. import { XenoCardFrame } from '@site/src/components/XenoCardFrame';

Anything here gets the riveted frame.

Never hardcode hex or rgb values anywhere in CSS or JSX. Always reference the --xeno-* CSS variables defined in src/css/custom.css.

Centers a short intro sentence directly under the page h1. Collapses its own bottom margin so it sits tight against whatever follows. import { DocsPageLead } from '@site/src/components/DocsPageLead'; # My Page <DocsPageLead>A one-liner that describes what this page is for.</DocsPageLead> ## First Section

Two-column layout: text on the left, a media card on the right. Stacks vertically on narrow viewports with the media below. The media prop takes any JSX, typically a <LocationCard /> or <HoverVideo />. import { DocsMediaRow } from '@site/src/components/DocsMediaRow'; <DocsMediaRow media={<LocationCard src="/img/something.png" title="The Panel" />}> Your step-by-step instructions here. The media card floats right at 220 px wide and aligns to the bottom of the text column. </DocsMediaRow>

Hover-aware wrapper for optional steps that have an accompanying video. Hovering the <HoverOption> block adds a warm left accent bar and plays the embedded <HoverVideo>. Omit src from <HoverVideo> to show a "Video coming soon" placeholder instead. import { HoverOption, HoverVideo } from '@site/src/components/HoverOption'; <HoverOption> <DocsMediaRow media={<HoverVideo src="/video/my-option.mp4" title="Right-click Menu" />}> 1. Your steps here... </DocsMediaRow> </HoverOption> The hover effect degrades gracefully to plain content if JS is unavailable.

These render inline replicas of VCC's own UI so prose instructions match what the reader sees. Import what you need: import { VccIcon, VccProjectsLabel, VccManageProjectLabel, AddIcon, RemoveIcon, VersionNone, VersionInstalled, } from '@site/src/components/InstallationInlineUi/InstallationInlineUi'; <VccIcon /> — the VCC favicon inline with text. Accepts a size prop (CSS value, default 1.2em). Open Creator Companion. Open <VccIcon /> **Creator Companion**. <VccProjectsLabel /> — the Projects sidebar entry as it appears in VCC, including the grid icon. Go to the Projects tab. Go to the <VccProjectsLabel /> tab. <VccManageProjectLabel /> — the Manage Project action label, styled like a small VCC button. Click Manage Project next to your project. Click <VccManageProjectLabel /> next to your project. <AddIcon /> and <RemoveIcon /> — the circular add and remove buttons from VCC's package list. Click to install, to remove. Click <AddIcon /> to install, <RemoveIcon /> to remove. <VersionNone /> and <VersionInstalled /> — the version dropdown pills from the VCC package list. If the version column shows none, the package isn't installed. Once installed it shows 1.2.3. If the version column shows <VersionNone />, the package isn't installed. Once installed it shows <VersionInstalled />.

Small inline icons matching the Unity editor's own file-type indicators. Use them next to any mention of a Unity asset type. import { SceneIcon, PrefabIcon, ModelIcon, PrefabModelIcon, PrefabVariantIcon, UnityPackageIcon, UnityPackage } from '@site/src/components/UnityIcon'; <SceneIcon /> <PrefabIcon /> <ModelIcon /> <PrefabModelIcon /> <PrefabVariantIcon /> <UnityPackageIcon /> Save your .unitypackage file somewhere you can find it. All icon components accept an optional size prop (number, pixels). Default is 16. Double-click the scene file <SceneIcon /> to open it. Drag the prefab <PrefabIcon /> into the Hierarchy. <UnityPackage /> combines the .unitypackage filename and icon into a single styled inline badge. Use it instead of writing `.unitypackage` <UnityPackageIcon />. Save your <UnityPackage /> file somewhere you can find it.

Every page is .mdx (not .md) so React components work inline. Frontmatter sets the sidebar position and title: --- sidebar_position: 2 title: My Page --- Imports go right after the frontmatter block, before any content.

Static images go in static/img/. In markdown prose, use the path as-is: ![alt text](/img/something.png) Inside a React component or JSX, always use useBaseUrl or the path will break in production: import useBaseUrl from '@docusaurus/useBaseUrl'; const src = useBaseUrl('/img/something.png');

Callout boxes for things that need to stand out. Keep them short — one or two sentences max. note note — neutral extra context that's helpful but not critical. Tag: :::note tip tip — shortcuts, recommendations, or things that make life easier. Tag: :::tip info info — background context the reader might not know. Tag: :::info caution caution — things that are easy to get wrong or miss. Also used as a placeholder marker for screenshots still needed. Tag: :::caution warning warning — things that can actually break something if ignored. Tag: :::warning danger danger — use sparingly, only for things with serious consequences. Tag: :::danger

The site CSS is split into six files loaded in dependency order from src/css/custom.css: theme-foundation.css — all --xeno-* CSS custom properties, base html/body rules, scrollbar styling, and text-wrap settings. This is the only place hex values should ever appear. theme-decor.css — the four fixed pseudo-element layers that create the framed decorative border on every page. Appearance is driven entirely by CSS variables, so per-page themes only need to override those variables. theme-docs.css — main content column: doc container background, h1/h2 heading styles, and the rules that hide placeholder markdown headings when a XenoMarkers component immediately follows them. theme-sidebar.css — sidebar shell, category frame cards with rivets, pill labels, the hover-highlight cursor, and the no-frame category modifier. theme-toc.css — right-hand table of contents panel, active cursor indicator, and the previous/next pagination cards. theme-chrome.css — breadcrumbs, navbar, footer (including the rivet decorations at the footer corners), and kbd/abbr overrides.

Each section of the wiki has its own color theme that changes the decorative border layers. Themes are defined in src/theme/shared/xenoPageTheme.ts and applied automatically on navigation — no MDX changes required. Path pattern data-xeno-decor Decor style Notes /docs/troubleshooting troubleshooting alt Yellow/olive palette, alternate mask images /docs/updating updating default Blue/purple palette /docs/customizing/** customizing default Default palette /docs/upload/** upload default Default palette Everything else default default Default warm orange/brown palette To add a new theme, add an entry to PAGE_THEME_DEFINITIONS in xenoPageTheme.ts: { pattern: /\/docs\/my-section(?:\/|$)/, decor: 'my-section', style: 'default', // 'default' or 'alt' — switches the mask image set variables: { '--xeno-page-bg-bottom': '#5ab2f2', '--xeno-page-decor-before-ramp-base': '#113357', '--xeno-page-decor-after-tl': 'rgb(197 220 237)', // ... }, }, style: 'alt' swaps in decor_top_alt.png, decor_bottom_alt.png, and decor_middle_alt.png. Use it if the default mask shapes don't suit the palette. Variable Controls --xeno-page-bg-bottom Bottom color of the full-page background gradient --xeno-page-bg-top Top color of the background gradient (defaults to --xeno-beige-light) --xeno-page-decor-before-ramp-base Base color of the top/bottom mask overlay --xeno-page-decor-before-ramp-highlight Highlight color within the mask overlay --xeno-page-decor-before-opacity Overall opacity of the html::before / body::before layers --xeno-page-decor-before-texture-shadow-blend Blend mode for the texture shadow --xeno-page-decor-after-tl/tr/bl/br Corner radial gradient colors in the center decor layer --xeno-page-decor-after-opacity Overall opacity of the html::after layer --xeno-page-decor-after-texture-blend Blend mode for the center texture layer --xeno-page-decor-after-ramp-base Base color of the ramp highlight layer --xeno-page-decor-after-ramp-highlight Highlight color for the ramp --xeno-page-decor-after-ramp-opacity Multiplied with the layer opacity
A reference for errors you're likely to run into when uploading or using avatars.

Cause: The selected object doesn't have a VRC Avatar Descriptor component, or no object is selected in the Builder tab. Fix: Select the root GameObject of your avatar in the scene, then open the SDK Builder tab again. Make sure a VRC Avatar Descriptor is attached to that object.

Cause: Often a script compilation error somewhere in the project that prevents Unity from building. Fix: Check the Unity Console (Window → General → Console) for any red errors. Fix all script errors before trying to upload. If errors are in third-party packages, try reimporting them via the Creator Companion.

If you get this error while entering play mode or attempting to upload the model that means you are missing either GoGoLoco or ADJerry's Facetracking Templates while using an older version of the Avatar. Please either update the Lucario Avatar or remove "FT- Lucario ReUnited UE FaceTracking Prefab" or "GogoLoco Beyond - Lucario ReUnited (VRCFury)" from the avatar in the Hierarchy. Compare your error to the images below to know which one to delete. GoGoLoco Error VRCFT Error
If your avatar appears as neon pink you most likely are missing the Poiyomi Shaders! In order to fix you will need to install Poiyomi (Follow this guide) Test Fixing Shaders

documents.t: Got a new version of your avatar? Whether the creator pushed an update or you just want to apply changes, here's how to get it into VRChat.

Download the updated avatar package from the creator, then import it into your Unity project by double-clicking the .unitypackage file (or dragging it into the Project window). Unity will ask which files to import — in most cases you can import everything. This overwrites the old avatar files in your project with the new ones.

Once the import is done, upload the avatar the same way you did the first time. Head over to the Uploading page if you need a refresher on the steps. tip You don't need to re-enter the name or description. VRChat remembers those from your first upload since you're updating the same avatar, not creating a new one. info Uploading overwrites the existing version of your avatar — no duplicates, it just updates the same one in your list.

If your avatar has a Quest version, make sure you upload that too — otherwise Quest users (including yourself on Quest) will still see the old version. Once you've uploaded for Windows, repeat the process and click Build & Publish for Android instead. The Quest and PC versions are already linked from your first upload, so you don't need to redo that part.
To get the avatar into Unity you need to import a Unity Package - a .unitypackage file that contains the model, textures, animations, and everything else the avatar needs.
Open the Creator Companion and go to the Projects tab. Click Open Project next to your project. Unity will launch, which can take a minute or two. info Unity is slow to open. Just let it load.
documents.s: Step 1 - Open your project in Unity

documents.t: You should have a .unitypackage file from your avatar download, named something like Lucario ReUnited VRC.unitypackage. ⚠️Put a screenshot of the right-click menu here Right-click Menu tip Not sure where it is? Check your Downloads folder, or wherever you saved it after downloading.
There are three ways to do this - pick whichever works for you:

The Project window is the panel at the bottom of Unity that shows all your project files. Inside it, you'll see a folder called Assets in the left sidebar. warning Project window vs Hierarchy These two panels are easy to mix up. The Hierarchy (left side of the screen) shows the objects in your current scene. The Project window (bottom) shows your files on disk. You want the Project window for this step. Right-click the Assets folder. Hover over Import Package. Click Custom Package.... Find your .unitypackage file in the file browser and select it. ▶Video coming soon Right-click Menu
documents.s: Option A - Right-click the Assets folder

documents.t: Open the folder where your .unitypackage file is saved. Drag the file on top of the Project window in Unity. Hold until the cursor changes, then let go. ▶Video coming soon Drag and Drop

Find the .unitypackage file in your file explorer. Double-click the .unitypackage. If Unity is open it will pick it up automatically. ▶Video coming soon Double-click Import Whichever method you used, Unity will show a list of everything in the package. Leave everything checked and click Import. caution Put an image of the Import dialog here Wait for the progress bar in the bottom-right corner to finish before doing anything else. info FBX import warnings may appear in the Console after importing. As long as the text is yellow and not red, they are safe to ignore.

Once the import finishes, navigate to this folder in the Project window: Assets / Monado_Art / Lucario ReUnited VRC / You may also notice a _MekenoTools folder in your Assets. It's a dependency that came with the avatar - just leave it alone, you don't need to touch it. Inside you'll find: The Scene - Double-click to open it. If you're new to Unity this is the easiest starting point since the avatar is already set up inside it. The Prefab - Drag it from the Project window into the Hierarchy to add it to your scene. The included scene has both prefabs placed in it side by side, so opening it first is a good way to see what each one looks like. There are two versions: Lucario ReUnited PC Prefab - the base version, with the Sir Aaron outfit and mohawk hair on by default. Lucario ReUnited PC Lite Prefab - this is the same base, but with a few things removed to get a better performance ranking. caution Put an image of the Project window showing the folder and files here
documents.s: Step 4 - Find the scene and prefab

documents.t: warning I know, you're probably very excited to start customizing the avatar right now, but hold off for just a bit! Do a clean upload first to make sure everything is working correctly before you start making changes. It's much easier to spot problems in a fresh import than after you've already modified things. Head to Uploading to get it into VRChat first.
To get an avatar into VRChat, you'll need to install a few things first. This page walks you through all of it step by step - no prior experience needed.​

warning If you just made your VRChat account, you will need to play the game or AFK in order to increase Trust Rank from Visitor to New User to upload avatars! Making friends can speed this up, or you can get VRC+ to receive New User rank immediately. Trust Ranks

The VRChat Creator Companion (usually called VCC) is a free program made by VRChat. Think of it as a control panel that helps you set up everything else. You install it once and it handles the rest. Go to vrchat.com and log in with your VRChat account. Click Downloads from the top menu. Download the Creator Companion and run the installer like you would any other program. When you open it for the first time, it will ask you to sign in with your VRChat account. Go ahead and do that. info If it asks for a verification code after signing in, check your email - VRChat sends one for security.

Unity is the program that actually lets you upload the avatar. VCC will prompt you to install it automatically, so you don't need to go hunting for the right version yourself. Open the Creator Companion. If Unity isn't installed yet, BCC will show a message asking you to install it. Click Install Unity. This opens a program called Unity Hub - it's just a launcher that manages Unity for you. Follow the prompts to finish installing. During setup, you'll be asked to create a free Unity account and activate a Personal license. This is completely free and just lets you use Unity. warning Don't install Unity yourself If you go to the Unity website and download it manually, you'll probably get the wrong version. VRChat is very picky about which version it supports - always let VCC install it for you. caution Already have Unity installed? You might have the wrong version. If you haven't updated VCC or Unity in a while, you may have Unity 2019 installed instead of the required Unity 2022. Using the wrong version will cause your project to break. To fix this: First, make sure your Creator Companion itself is up to date - check for updates and install them if available. Open the Creator Companion and go to Settings in the bottom-left corner. Click the General tab. If you see a pop-up or banner that says something like "Recommended Version Not Installed", click Install Now. Wait for Creator Companion to finish installing the correct version. Once Unity 2022 is installed, you're good to go.

A project is just a folder on your computer where all your avatar files will live. You create and manage it through the Creator Companion. Open the Creator Companion and click Projects in the sidebar on the left. Click the blue Create New Project button in the top right. From the template list, select "Unity 2022 Avatar Project". Give your project a name and choose where to save it. tip Choose a sensible save location By default, VCC might try to save it inside a hidden system folder (AppData). It's better to save it somewhere easy to find, like Documents\VRChat Projects\ or similar. Click Create and wait for it to finish. This might take a minute or two.

Before you can install anything, VCC needs to know where to find these packages. Click Add to VCC on each card below. Once you've clicked all four, a message will appear at the bottom telling you what to do next. Mandatory Dependencies VRCFury Automatically sets up complex avatar features so you don't have to do it manually. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://vcc.vrcfury.com Poiyomi Toon The shader used for the avatar's materials. Without it, the avatar will appear completely pink. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://poiyomi.github.io/vpm/index.json Optional - but heavily recommended ⚠️ These packages are not strictly required, but pay close attention during the upload process. If you choose to skip them, missing packages can produce errors and cause the upload to fail. ADJerry's Face Tracking Templates Adds face tracking support to the avatar. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://Adjerry91.github.io/VRCFaceTracking-Templates/index.json GoGoLoco Adds movement options like sitting and laying down anywhere in VRChat. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://Spokeek.github.io/goloco/index.json info You only need to do this once per package, ever. Once a source is added to VCC, it stays there for all future projects.
documents.s: Step 4 - Add the package sources to VCC

documents.t: Now that VCC knows where the packages are, you need to install them into your project. This is the step that puts them in your Unity project and makes them usable. Open Creator Companion and click Projects in the sidebar on the left. Find your project in the list and click Manage Project. You'll see a list of packages. Find each of the following and click the button next to them: VRCFury(Required) - Used to put the avatar together. Poiyomi Toon(Required) - Used for shadersMake sure you pick Toon, not Pro! - Pro is paid and won't work if you don't own it! VRCFT - Jerry's Templates(Optional) - Used for Face Tracking GoGoLoco(Optional) - Used for flight and body poses without FullBody Tracking Wait for VCC to finish installing each one - it may take a moment. info You'll know it worked when the version box changes from none to a version number (e.g. 1.2.3), and the button changes to .
documents.s: Step 5 - Install the packages into your project

documents.t: Once everything is installed, head to Unity Basics to learn how to navigate Unity or skip to Uploading if you are already familiar with Unity!

tip Already know Unity? If you've used Unity before and feel comfortable navigating it, feel free to skip straight to Uploading. When you open your project for the first time, Unity can look pretty overwhelming. There are panels everywhere and none of it is obvious. This page breaks down what each part of the screen does so you're not flying blind.

When Unity first opens, you'll see something like this: Unity Editor Layout Each section is its own panel, and you can resize or rearrange them. Don't worry if yours looks slightly different - Unity lets you move things around.

Where: Top-left panel. Hirearchy Hierarchy Panel The Hierarchy is a list of everything that exists in your current scene. Think of it like a folder tree - objects can be nested inside other objects. For avatar work, this is where you'll find your avatar. It will usually appear as a single entry that you can click the arrow next to expand and see all its parts (bones, meshes, etc.). When you click something in the Hierarchy, it gets selected and it's details show up in the Inspector on the right. Hierarchy - Inspector Link

Where: Right-side panel. Inspector Inspector Panel The Inspector shows you the details of whatever you have selected. If you click on your avatar in the Hierarchy, the Inspector will show all the components attached to it - things like the Avatar Descriptor (which tells VRChat this is an avatar) and any other settings. You'll interact with the Inspector a lot when following guides, since most settings are changed here. info If you click somewhere and the Inspector goes blank or shows something unexpected, you probably just accidentally selected the wrong thing. Go back to the Hierarchy and click what you actually wanted.

Where: Large panel in the center. Scene Scene View The Scene View is a 3D viewport where you can see and move around your avatar visually. You can think of it like a free camera flying around your scene. Basic controls: Right-click + drag - Rotate the camera Right-click + WASD - Fly through the scene (hold right-click, then move with WASD) Right-click + Q/E - Move the camera down/up while flying Middle-click + drag - Pan the camera Scroll wheel - Zoom in/out Press F (with something selected) - Focus the camera on that object caution TODO Mention scroll speed and shift to speed up flying Scene View Navigation For uploading, you don't really need to move things around in the Scene View - just knowing how to navigate it is enough.

Where: Usually tabbed behind the Scene View (click the "Game" tab to switch). Game View The Game View shows what the camera inside the scene sees - basically a preview of what things would look like in-game. For avatar uploading you won't use this much.

Where: Bottom panel. Project Project Window The Project window is your file browser. It shows all the files that make up your project - textures, materials, scripts, prefabs, and so on. Think of it like File Explorer, but only showing the contents of your project folder. When you import your avatar files, they'll appear here. You can double-click folders to open them, and drag files from the Project window into the Hierarchy to add them to your scene. Project - Hierarchy Drag

Where: Usually tabbed next to the Project window (click "Console" to switch). Console The Console shows messages from Unity - information, warnings, and errors. White messages - General info, usually safe to ignore. Yellow messages - Warnings. Often harmless, but worth noting. Red messages - Errors. These mean something is actually wrong and usually need to be fixed before you can upload. If your upload fails or something breaks, the Console is the first place to check. tip If you see a wall of red errors when you first open your project, don't panic. Make sure all four packages from the Installation step are properly installed - missing packages are the most common cause.

Where: Very top of the window. Toolbar The row of menus across the top (File, Edit, Assets, GameObject, Component, VRChat SDK, Window, Help) works like any other program. The one you'll use most is VRChat SDK, which is where you open the upload panel.
Now that you know your way around, head to Uploading to get your avatar into VRChat.

This page covers how to upload your avatar using the VRChat SDK inside Unity. Make sure you've completed the Installation steps before continuing. Outfits and other customization options are covered in the Customizing section.

In Unity, go to the top menu bar and click: VRChat SDK → Show Control Panel caution Put an image of where to find it This opens the SDK window. If you don't see this menu, the SDK probably isn't installed correctly - go back to the Creator Companion and make sure the VRChat SDK package is added to your project.

In the SDK window, go to the Authentication tab and sign in with your VRChat account. tip Sign in with your email address, not your username. Username logins don't tend to work as reliably in the SDK. note You may be prompted for a two-factor authentication code. Check your email.

Switch to the Builder tab at the top of the SDK window. In the Selected Avatar dropdown, choose your avatar. The SDK will run a few checks on your avatar. Fix any errors shown in red before continuing. Warnings (yellow) are usually safe to ignore.

Fill in the Avatar Name and give it a Thumbnail. Description and tags are entirely optional. Scroll down in the Builder tab. Make sure Build & Publish your Avatar Online is selected as the Build Type and Windows is selected in the Platform dropdown. Wait for Unity to build the avatar. Depending on how many components you have added, this can take a few minutes. If successful, you will see a message saying Build Successful in green text. Once finished, your avatar will appear in VRChat under My Avatars.

If you want to upload a Mobile compatible version, you need to link it to the same pipeline ID as the PC version so they're uploaded onto the same avatar. Find the prefab for the Mobile version of the avatar and drag it into the hierarchy, add the same additions as you did on the PC version. In the SDK's Content Manager tab, find your uploaded PC avatar and click Copy ID. In your scene, select the root object of the Quest avatar. Find the Pipeline Manager component on it. Paste the copied ID into the Blueprint ID field and click Attach. Now repeat the upload steps above using Build & Publish Your Avatar Online with Android selected in the Platform dropdown. caution If the mobile avatar is not uploaded onto the same Blueprint ID as the PCVR version, they will be treated as two entirely different avatar uploads. This means that if you are on PCVR, your Quest standalone friends wont see your avatar and vice-versa.
If something goes wrong during the upload, check the Troubleshooting page for common errors and fixes.
If the upload went through, nice work! If you want to start customizing the avatar - outfits, accessories, that sort of thing - head over to the Customizing section.
